purpose: Quantify how the aligned versus anti-aligned state contrast propagates to realised functional-loss incidence across fixed future horizons, while separately showing how uncertainty contracts as paired replication increases.

relationship_to_phase_v.legacy_result: The original preregistered Phase V remains frozen at 60 generations and 500 paired trajectories.

future_forcing.rule: At generation g, barrier = 0.50 + (0.65-0.50)*g/60. Horizons truncate this one common per-generation forcing path; the schedule is not rescaled to end at 0.65 at shorter horizons.

paired_replication.pairing: Aligned and anti-aligned trajectories use the same deterministic trajectory seed for each master-seed/replicate index, exactly as in Phase V.

estimands.primary: For each horizon at 1500 pairs, anti-aligned minus aligned realised functional-loss risk difference with a paired large-sample 95% confidence interval.
secondary: The same paired risk difference and interval at nested 500- and 1000-pair prefixes as a precision audit.
Discordant pair counts and exact McNemar p values as secondary descriptions, not acceptance gates.
Loss-time direction among trajectories observed by the maximum horizon as a descriptive timing layer.
estimands.no_significance_search: No horizon or pair count is selected post hoc by the smallest p value. All 4 x 3 cells are reported.

planning_power.role: Planning only; power is not an acceptance criterion and is not recomputed after seeing propagation outcomes.

decision_language.allowed: Report the effect-size trajectory and interval at every declared horizon. If intervals contract around a horizon-dependent pattern, describe the supported propagation timescale quantitatively.
forbidden: Do not call a horizon the true cutoff solely because p crosses 0.05.
Do not alter the forcing schedule, state values, seeds, horizons or pair-count grid after outcomes are opened.
Do not pool nested pair-count prefixes as independent experiments.
Do not relabel this post-Phase-V experiment as preregistered Phase V.
